first_prompt:
Review and implement `~/code/scripts/analysis/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-brief.md`. Use your judgment on how you approach the work to maximize quality and efficiency.

The brief for this work is `llm-dl

commits.summary: Add the private archive of original outputs: spool, journal, verified upload, list and fetch
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py is the first piece of the process-plumbing brief (llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing.md, section 2). A producer hands the bytes it made to capture before it shortens, replaces or deletes them. They are sealed once into a spool on disk outside the checkout (~/.local/share/in-the-loop/originals), with a full private inventory of every member's path, type, mode, length and SHA-256, and acknowledged only after the intake record and a SQLite journal have them durably. Small files go into bounded packs, large ones into parts, and an append-only file into segments from which any past prefix restores. A restartable uploader commits each attempt before a byte moves, creates each object only if none is there, reads it back with a credential and compares the original bytes with their name, and writes an immutable receipt last, so a fresh machine can rebuild the catalog from the store alone. Ordinary and restricted originals go to separate private R2 buckets; a restricted occurrence is listed in the ordinary one by a stub with no path. list, show and fetch read with the reader's token into a private cache and work offline on a verified hit; missing, pending, restricted or damaged evidence gives a specific unavailable answer. Nothing in the tool deletes a byte, and ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1 switches capture off.

Verified by 33 unit tests (llm-dlc/tools/test_artifacts.py): crashes before and after the intake record, after a put and before the receipt, a lease left by a dead worker, two workers on one object, a store that is offline, that loses its answer, that holds other bytes under the same key or a truncated object, a full disk, reused paths, gaps, unsafe manifests and links, and reads from an empty cache and offline. artifacts.py canary passed 11 of 11 checks on the real buckets on 2026-11-21: custody for both classes, a restore from an empty cache, and each token's limits (the ordinary token refused a restricted key, a PUT and a DELETE; the public Worker and the public traces' token read neither class). The contract is in llm-dlc/specification.md, Original outputs; llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md records where the run stands. Nothing calls capture yet: the runner and collector adapters come next.

commits.summary: Seal each verification run's originals before the pipeline cuts or removes them (shadow mode)
commits.body:
verification/capture.py hands what the runner and the collector produce to the private archive (llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py) at the points where an original was lost until now: the whole step logs before they are cut to head and tail, the outputs with the declared ones that never materialized and the ones deleted, the whole changes.diff, what a failed job's work directory holds beyond its commit, the result as the runner wrote it, a collected result that a later collect replaces, a result staged by a runner that sealed nothing, and the result as collected with its conflicts. A run directory left by an attempt whose runner was killed is sealed as partial before the retry reuses its path, and each run of a job is a numbered attempt. result.json names the attempt and the occurrence ids under a new originals field (in the schema).

It is a shadow of the pipeline: verification/results holds what it held before, pipeline.py gains four calls and a loader, and a capture that fails (a full disk, say) fails no job and no collect, is said on stderr and in .state/capture.log, and makes collect set a staged result aside under .state/uncaptured instead of deleting it. The test runner and test_pipeline.py set ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1, so no test seals anything into this machine's archive. artifacts.capture gained sparse, for the work directory's rule.

Verified by verification/test_capture.py (7 tests, each running the pipeline in a throwaway repository with its own spool and store): the middle of a log the result cut restores byte for byte from a fresh cache; a failed job's outputs, diff and work-directory additions restore, and its never-made output is recorded; collect seals the result it replaces and the one it writes, with conflicts; a disk-full capture leaves the job passed, the collect done and the staged files set aside. The tests the change selects passed (35 files, after updating the one that pins the runner's environment). verification/README.md, Originals, describes it.

commits.summary: Inventory and protect what exists only on this VM; upload sealed originals in parallel
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/vm_inventory.py is the brief's first step. measure prints numbers fit to publish (heads, unpushed commits, git and jj sizes, tracked files and the widest directories, the runner's state, transcripts, run records, what a push would send, the archive's custody), to be compared before and after each change to the plumbing. pin writes a git ref under refs/itl/pins/ for every local head origin lacks, a namespace jj neither imports nor moves. protect seals into the private archive the runner's run directories and kept work directories, the loops' private run records, the project's source transcripts (Claude Code's and Codex's, as append-only streams, with their side files) and the records of examples 340 to 359, and does not seal twice what has not changed. It names only this repository's folders: no other project's sessions, credential store or dependency cache is read.

On 2026-11-21 it sealed 1,182 occurrences on this VM in two minutes: 3.21 GB of originals as 541 MB in 2,522 objects, among them 910 run directories and the 23,000 record files of runs 5 to 7, whole, before any trim (VF-053). All 8 local heads are pinned. llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md has the measurements, what was left unsealed and why, and the known historical gaps.

The uploader now works on up to 8 threads, each with its own journal connection, writes an intent for each new occurrence first, and reads back every object and every receipt; upload --drain runs passes until nothing is left to do now, as the spool's one uploader (a lock), and artifacts.kick starts one in the background when a run or a collect seals something, so the transfer off the machine starts then. Verified by three new tests in test_artifacts.py (12 occurrences on 4 threads, each object put once; the lock; the kick's switches), test_vm_inventory.py (sealed once, again only on change; a dry run seals nothing; only this repository's transcript folders are named), and the tests the change selects (5 files, test_pipeline.py among them).

commits.summary: Add sync.py checkpoint: one committed revision to origin's develop, forward only, with outgoing-object checks
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/checkpoint.py gives code checkpoints a job of their own, apart from promotion (the brief, section 1). sync.py checkpoint --rev REV resolves REV once to one committed revision, reads the remote's develop and main, and pushes exactly SHA:refs/heads/develop to origin when develop can move forward to it, carrying the commit develop was read at so the push cannot land on a branch that moved. It runs no test, renders no trace file, uploads no log and waits for no job or uploader, and every jj call it makes ignores the working copy, so another session's uncommitted files are neither snapshotted nor moved. --bootstrap creates develop where main is. Any other ref, remote, pattern or force is refused as an argument.

Before anything leaves the machine it reads every git object and commit message the push would expose for the first time, through every outgoing commit and merge parent, and refuses an unresolved conflict, a raw payload path, an unsafe file name, a blob over 16 MiB, a message-less or set-aside commit, a recognisable credential or one of this machine's own secrets or account identifiers anywhere, anything the redactor would still change in a trace file, and a redaction decision no person is recorded as having taken. A scan of the 18 commits then unpushed showed why the context-shaped kinds are refused in trace files only: the home path and the user name occur in 5,153 result and receipt files of the kind main already publishes, and KEY=value in 109 ordinary fixtures. A blob's verdict is kept by its git id under the policy, rules and decisions in force. A push whose answer is lost is settled by reading the remote. The receipt, outside the tree and sealed into the private archive, says which trace logs are public and which pending and what the archive holds on this machine only. After a push, develop@origin counts among jj's immutable heads.

The redactor now also treats the private archive's three R2 tokens as this machine's secrets. Verified by llm-dlc/tools/test_checkpoint.py, 12 tests on real jj repositories with a bare remote: a dirty workspace is checkpointed at its last commit with the foreign files' hashes and the working-copy commit unchanged, a fresh clone reads the code at develop, and the test gate, the session sync and the log upload are each patched to fail if called; a credential in a parent commit is refused though the tip deleted it; an unsafe message, a run record, an environment file, an oversized blob, a bad name, a conflict and a forged allow-list approval are refused with the remote unchanged; --all, --bookmark, --force, --remote, a refspec and a pattern exit 2; a develop that moved elsewhere is never forced; a lost answer is one push. The tests the change selects passed (22 files). llm-dlc/specification.md, Checkpoints, is the contract. The first push to the real develop is the watcher's, at this cycle's end (the user's decision); a rehearsal on the real history against a bare remote follows. The allow list gains one proposal (a82875ef, a made-up home directory in test_vm_inventory.py), for the user to approve.

commits.summary: Seal source transcripts at each sync; reproduce example 359's native-selector route from hydrated evidence
commits.body:
sync.py now hands each synced session's source transcript, and its subagents', to the private archive as an append-only stream in restricted custody (seal_transcripts): what the file gained since it was last sealed, so a commit seals the turns that led to it and the upload starts then. Only a file in a client's own session store is sealed, and an error there goes to the hook log and fails no sync. artifacts.transcript_key names the streams, as vm_inventory.py protect did.

The archive's list was slow on first use, one request a receipt for 1,182 receipts: it now reads what it lacks on 16 threads, and on the capturing machine takes from the journal the receipts that machine wrote (1.5 s). Occurrence ids now carry the microsecond before their random bits, so they sort in the order they were made; a test had shown two made in one second in either order.

The brief's exercise on evidence semantics, run on the line's commit 7d865e55 with an empty cache and the reader's token: example 359's records (6,374 files, 97.5 MB) restored from the store into a plain export in 2.5 s, and the run directory of job 20261121-155348-repeat-organic-java-example-359-on-the-f (5,905 files, 64.6 MB) in 1.8 s, both identical to the checkout by diff -r; workflow_handoff.py handoff 359 --revision fix there reported contents-fix native selectors established, 2,865 admitted, 2,865 checked, no first blocker, and the same routes and coverage as in the checkout; with one native.json removed, then with one byte changed, that record became ineligible while the other record and the four finite-JVM routes stayed established. llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md records it, with the rehearsal of sync.py checkpoint on the real history against a bare remote on disk (0.9 to 2.3 s for one commit, 15.0 s for 17 commits and 5,877 new blobs, the working copy unread).

Verified by two new tests in test_artifacts.py (a synced session sealed as streams with its subagent, a file outside a client's store left alone, a second sync sealing only what was gained; sealing never fails a sync), by test_artifacts.py, test_vm_inventory.py, test_checkpoint.py and test_capture.py run again after the last edits, and by the tests the change to sync.py selects (22 files).

commits.summary: Cut the entry points over to checkpoints: the default run belongs to a promotion, not to a landing
commits.body:
The brief asks that the watcher stop pausing for the old checklist. CLAUDE.md, llm-dlc/README.md, the operating notes, the brief template and the /single-agent-run, /multi-agent-brief and /publish skills now say the same thing: a checkpoint (sync.py checkpoint --rev REV) puts a committed revision on origin's develop with no test run, no log upload and no wait, and is the watcher's to make without asking, at a finished slice, when a stream or a run lands, at a pause or when a snapshot is asked for; main moves by a promotion, at the user's word. Since 2026-11-21 the default test run is owed at a promotion to main and at a release only, each of which runs it itself when no passed run covers the commit. It is no longer owed when an example is done, when a stream or a run lands, or after a merge; an agent still runs it when it answers a development question, with default_run.py after-merge. The tests of what changed before each commit stay as they were.

CLAUDE.md also says how to find and restore originals from the private archive and who reads which class, and the operating notes gain a section on checkpoints and the archive (never force, published commits are immutable, check custody before removing a run directory by hand, tests seal nothing). The Claude Code permissions deny reading the archive's token files or naming their path in a command; no allow rule was added for the checkpoint, which the watcher's session already runs as it runs the other watcher tools. Codex's rules cannot express a denied path and are unchanged.

vm_inventory.py protect now leaves the runner's mark in each run directory it seals, so a rerun of the job does not take the directory for an attempt nobody sealed; it wrote the mark into the 910 directories sealed earlier without sealing anything again. llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md has the acceptance table as it stands after this cycle, what is left in order, and notes for the next cycle. Verified by the tests the documentation changes select (17 files, test_claude_setup.py and test_release.py among them) and test_vm_inventory.py.

commits.summary: Record the design of sync.py promote for the next cycle
commits.body: llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md gains the design of the promotion command as settled against the code in cycle 1: the frozen set from the remote's main and the named develop commit, one standing candidate workspace moved with jj new, the metadata as a commit of its own made by that checkout's own tools, the missing-receipt check, the gate with one narrow exemption for the README's generated session table, the forward-only pushes with the expected main, the summary under llm-dlc/artifacts, and the tests to write. Bookkeeping only: no code changed and no test was run.

commits.summary: Add sync.py promote: a frozen part of develop becomes main, with its logs, originals and test receipt accounted for
commits.body:
A promotion is now a command of its own (llm-dlc/tools/promote.py, the specification's new Promotions section). It takes a commit that is already on origin's develop, freezes the commits between main and it (merge parents included; what lands on develop later waits for the next promotion), and builds the publication record in a jj workspace of its own, REPO-promote, so it runs from any workspace whatever is uncommitted there. In the candidate the frozen commits' logs are taken from the workspaces that store them, checked and uploaded; every LLM-Trace must then resolve to a published or withdrawn log, and every original of the frozen jobs, sessions and commits must be remote_verified in the private archive or be a job with no original at all, which is counted as a gap. The record is one commit on the frozen commit holding generated files only: the URLs, the index, and llm-dlc/artifacts/YYYY/MM/DD/promotion-ID.json, a summary of at most 64 KiB (llm-dlc/publication-summary.schema.json) that names the private inventory by occurrence and SHA-256.

The gate asks for a passed default run covering the record's tree, and runs it in the candidate when none does. default_run.covers now also passes llm-dlc/artifacts/ and a llm-dlc/README.md that differs only in its generated session table (the page's own text is still covered), so a run of the frozen commit's tree covers the record. The gate's record and log are sealed in the archive and must be verified there before main moves; the receipt is outside the tree. main is pushed only if it is still where the promotion found it, forward only, and a lost answer is settled by reading the remote; develop then goes forward to the record, or takes it in by an ordinary merge when it moved meanwhile. The state of a promotion is kept by base and frozen commit, so the same command continues one that stopped and finishes one whose push went out before its end was written. --dry-run prints the review view (source changes by finished change, the test receipt, decisions, logs and originals by state) and changes nothing.

commits.summary: Checkpoint: a credential fixture the remote already holds is not refused again when its file is edited
commits.body:
The rehearsal of sync.py promote on this line's real history refused the checkpoint of the promote commit itself: that commit edits llm-dlc/tools/test_performance.py, a redaction test that has carried a made-up private key since before main's head, git names the edited file as a new blob, and the scan refused it. A blob's findings are now compared with those of the same file at the push's bases (the remote's develop and main): when every kind and value is already there, the edit exposes nothing new and the blob passes, counted as carried in the receipt; a value the base's copy does not hold is refused as before.

Also in promote.py: a trailer whose session's manifest is not in the frozen tree says what resolves it (the workspace that ran the session lands, and that commit is promoted), and the review view counts examples' replay records with the generated records rather than as source lines. Verified by test_checkpoint.py (13 tests, one new: the edit passes, a second token in the same file is refused and not printed) and test_promote.py.

commits.summary: Add delegated redaction decisions, switched off: a person can let one run's watcher decide routine findings
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/delegation.py and the specification's new Delegated decisions paragraph under Redaction. Nothing changes until a person turns it on: the watcher asks with sync.py delegate request, the person grants that request from their own terminal, and sync.py delegate off ends it from any shell. The watcher is the client process (Claude Code's or Codex's) that asked, by pid, start time and boot: a command is the watcher's when the nearest client process above it is that one, so an environment variable or a file in the checkout confers nothing, a worker the watcher started is not the watcher, and a watcher that ended decides nothing more.

While it is on the watcher has three commands of its own, spelled apart from the person's so that the project's permission rules for those stay as they are. delegate approve takes allow-list proposals by id with evidence the command checks itself (the value is in a file main publishes, in a committed fixture, is a digest of a committed file, a git object id or a log's name); a stated public origin is recorded as not checked and refused for a long-token; the kinds the redactor removes stay refused. delegate withhold keeps an unpublished log out of publication for good: sealed in the restricted archive, removed, marked withdrawn in its manifest. delegate mask adds a value to this machine's redactions, withholds the unpublished logs that hold it and escalates the published ones. review escalate (anyone) writes one masked record that check warns of until a person closes it. No command prints a value.

Each decision is a line of a record outside every checkout, chained by hash, signed with a key the permission rules deny agents, and sealed into the restricted archive as it grows. check, land, checkpoint and promote count a decision when it is on main, recorded as a person's, or recorded by the watcher with exactly the bytes the file has, under the redaction policy in force, while the delegation is on. A decision now counts as published only on main: before, any immutable commit counted, and commits on develop have been immutable since the checkpoint command. Also here: promote abandons a record it committed and then found wanting, and does not count its own records among a promotion's evidence; the results page records the promotion rehearsal on the real history (25 commits promoted on a bare remote, the checkpoint fix and the three real missing receipts it found), where a commit's 28 s go, and the design of the trace changes that are next.

Verified by test_delegation.py (9 tests: off by default; who the watcher is; an approval with checked evidence; the refusals; a forged entry, changed bytes, an added and an edited record line, a stale policy and delegation off all failing; withholding into restricted custody; masking with one escalation) and by test_costs.py run --changed (25 files passed).

commits.summary: Render the generated trace files at promotion, not at every commit; make the check after a commit four times faster
commits.body:
An ordinary sync.py commit, and the commit hook, now write the session's manifest alone. Until now each commit also rewrote the session's summary.md and metrics.json and six global files (index.json, the table in llm-dlc/README.md, traces/README.md, traces/metrics.json, traces/loops.json, traces/loops.md): twelve generated files a commit, megabytes of them for a long session, and a conflict in the global ones whenever two lines merged. They are rendered when they are published or asked for: by sync.py promote in its candidate workspace (from each session's stored current log and its manifest, which now records the workspace path a summary shortens file names by), by sync.py push, and on demand by sync.py sync, also spelled sync.py render, and sync.py regenerate. A session's first commit still makes its summary and metrics, so links to them resolve, and a session synced without rendering is rendered by the next sync that renders whether or not it changed. check compares the generated files with their inputs only when asked (check --rendered, as a promotion and a push ask); it always scans them, and always checks manifests, logs and trailers. The specification's Workflow section has a Rendering paragraph.

A new commit carries LLM-Trace: SESSION sha256:LOG and no longer the two link lines above it, LLM-Trace-Summary (a URL on main) and LLM-Trace-Log (the CDN's URL), which were promises about a promotion that had not happened. Commits that have them keep them, no published commit is restamped, and every reader takes either form. sync.py trace REV says what a commit's identifier resolves to now: the session, its summary, and its log, public, withdrawn, or pending and in which workspace it waits.

The check after a commit took about 16 s of a commit's 28 s here. Two things took half of it. check_trailers read a manifest out of the tree of every traced commit there has ever been (1,543 here): it now keeps what it read of immutable commits, by checkout and tools version, and asks jj only for what @ gained since and for the mutable commits; when a recorded head is no longer an immutable ancestor of @, or under --full, everything is read again. And every stored log's .gz bytes were hashed again at each check to find its cache entry: a log is named by its content and never rewritten, so it is now found by path, size, time and inode, except by an upload, which goes by the bytes it sends, and under --full. Measured here, warm: check 4.1 s (trailers 5.7 s to 0.4 s, sessions 9.5 s to 2.6 s).

Verified by test_performance.py (two tests of rendering on demand, two of the trailer and its resolver; the two tests that pinned the old behaviour updated), test_workspaces.py (the cursor on a real jj repository: read once, still judged against the manifests as they are now, dropped when the commit stops being published, not used under a full audit) and test_costs.py run --changed (23 files passed).

commits.summary: Find a verification job and its result by id, kept flat or under its day: every reader goes through verification/layout.py
commits.body:
The brief's pipeline layout, readers first. verification/layout.py is the one place that knows where a job's specification and its result are: flat (verification/jobs/ID.json, verification/results/ID/), as all 986 are, or under the UTC day the id begins with (verification/jobs/YYYY/MM/DD/ID.json), with one overflow shard for an id without a date. A job is never moved, since the runner tests the commit that last touched its file; a result goes beside its job; identical duplicates resolve to the flat copy and differing ones are named by pipeline.py validate. Results recorded on other heads are recognised in both layouts from a listing of the commit's tree.

Readers moved to it: pipeline.py (the queue, status, collect, commit-paths, report, resubmit, prioritize, validate, the results index, schema references at the new depth), sync.py's loop statistics, cost_inventory.py, conductor.py, brief_run.py, accept.py, claim_history.py, capture.py, vm_inventory.py and promote.py. New jobs still go flat (WRITE = "flat" in layout.py; VERIFY_LAYOUT=shards for one command): the brief migrates readers before writers, and two standing decisions of the user say to add no complexity to pipeline.py and to move no folders, so the switch is one line left for a person after a real promotion. The conductor loads the module only for the one question that needs it, so a copy of the loop's scripts in a checkout without it still answers the others.

Also fixed, found by this very commit: sync.py commit --only named every file it set aside on one jj command line, and 16,000 of them (an example's per-case records, being packed for the next commit) were more than a command line holds. It now names what stays, and prints the first 40 of a long list with the count of the rest.

commits.summary: Keep an example's per-case records as one pack a folder, read in place; hold the records to a budget in check
commits.body:
The records' rule of VF-053 (the user's decision 5: seal the records, show 359 restores, then slim them by rule). A native-selector run writes two files for each admitted selector; over examples 340 to 359 that was 16,376 of the 22,103 files their records held, one folder with 2,865 entries. examples/tools/targets/case_pack.py keeps such a folder as cases.tar.gz beside where it was: the same bytes under the same names, written so that the same files give the same pack. The validator (native_selectors.validate_result) reads a case from the folder or from the pack and compares its digest either way, so a plain checkout checks every case as before and nothing has to be fetched from the private archive, which a public reader cannot read. A selector run packs its own output at its end.

Applied in one pass to examples 341, 345, 347, 354 and 359: 16,376 files became 45 packs (37.0 MB to 0.9 MB), the twenty examples' records went from 22,103 files to 5,772, and no folder has more than 1,000 entries. Shown: each of the five handoffs (workflow_handoff.py handoff NNN, and --revision fix for 354 and 359) is byte for byte what it was; the five sealed originals restored from the store with artifacts.py fetch equal the packed records file for file (case_pack.py verify --against, 16,376 members); with one packed case of 359 removed, and then with one byte of it changed, its record became ineligible (does not exist; different raw checker output) while the other 39 established results stayed, and matched again with the pack put back; validate_example.py passes for the five. Not cut: the bytes of the large per-execution files (execution.json, 125 MB in 319 files), which are few and read whole; what to keep of them is a question about the evidence, for the user.

The budget: sync.py check reports more than 50 loose per-case files in one cases/ folder as an error that names the command, and more than 2,000 files under one example's records/ or 1,000 entries in one folder as a warning (none of either now; 50 ms). It also warns at 100 commits on neither develop nor main. The checkpoint's scan now reads a gzip blob as what it opens to, every member and whatever follows the last, and refuses one that opens to more than 256 MiB: without that, a credential inside a pack would have left unseen (POLICY 3, so each kept verdict is worked out once more).

Also in this commit, from the brief's acceptance table and VF-053: a test that kills the collector (SIGKILL) with a result's folder wiped and again with the result written, and collects again, with the earlier result sealed before the wipe; the watcher's private analysis reads an occurrence its machine never held from the store alone (shown on a disk store; on the real restricted bucket it is the watcher's to run); prune_workspaces.py counts a file as recoverable when the archive holds its exact bytes verified in the store, and its tests no longer read the machine's own archive; both run skills have the watcher say, with each verdict or merge, what waits on a person. VF-053 records what was done against each of its needs and stays open for the user.

commits.summary: Record the run report; a promotion stopped by a fault of the tools says so; Codex may not switch delegation on
commits.body:
The results page of the plumbing run gains its report at the end of cycle 2: no real promotion was made (it is at the user's word; origin/main is unchanged and origin/develop holds cycle 1 since the watcher's first checkpoint), the archive's inventory and the restores shown, timings before and after, the custody gaps still open, and the paths and commands a later reorganisation has to keep. It also records a second rehearsal of the whole line against a bare remote on disk, with the record rendered in the candidate by the new code: 27 commits checkpointed in one scan of 12.7 s, the commit that packs the records opened and scanned in 3.0 s, a dry run with no blocker, and a promotion whose record of 15 files put main and develop at the same commit; check --rendered in the candidate reported 0 errors.

Two small changes came out of that rehearsal and the review of the leftovers. promote.py: when the candidate's side stops on an exception that is not a refusal, the promotion's state now records it as the reason, as it does for a refusal, and the same command continues the same promotion (the first attempt of the rehearsal stopped on the harness's own outdated stand-in and left no reason). .codex/rules: switching delegated redaction on is forbidden to Codex as it is to Claude Code; the watcher's own forms stay open.

commits.summary: Queue the selector route of example 345 on the commit that packs a run's per-case output (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261121-194629-345-native-selectors-again-the-run-packs: the four parent-fix tasks of example 345 by complete native case analysis, as job 20261120-213848-345-parent-fix-exhaust-native-selector-b ran them, now that a selector run replaces each cases/ folder of its record with cases.tar.gz at its end and the validator reads a case from the folder or the pack. Its second step fails if any per-case folder is left loose or the records are over their budget; its third reads the example's claim history and fails if it cites no record of the run or reports a case missing, altered or unreadable. About 3 minutes and 140 MiB by the earlier run.

Why a job: the checker is a proof-tier tool and does not run inline. Until the result is in, the packing at the end of a run rests on the pack's own tests and on the five examples packed after the fact; the results page says so.

commits.summary: Keep the verification results index by day for results kept by day
commits.body: The brief's 'partition the result index': verification/results/index.json lists the results kept flat and names, under shards, each day that has results of its own; such a day has its own index.json with the same lines for its results. So once new jobs go by day the first file stops growing, and is the complete index of everything collected before the switch; a day's index is rewritten only by that day's collects. With no sharded result, as today, the file is byte for byte what the writer produced before (checked on the real 986 results: identical, 1,158,583 bytes).

commits.summary: Queue example 345's selector route again, requiring the built checker (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261121-195020-345-native-selectors-with-the-built-chec replaces 20261121-194629-345-native-selectors-again-the-run-packs, whose pass shows nothing: I had not declared that the job requires jvmcontract, so its run ended in 0.4 s with 'no built native checker', and its three checks accepted that (an exit of 1 is also what a real run with refuted claims ends with, and the newest record cited by the claim history was an old one). The new job requires java, javac and jvmcontract, and its first step fails unless the run left a record newer than the newest the commit holds, with the page task's result in it; the second fails unless that record holds a pack and no loose per-case folder; the third fails unless the claim history cites that record and reports no case missing, altered or unreadable.

The results page names the first job's pass for what it is. The packing at the end of a selector run stays unshown by a real run of the checker until this job is in.

commits.summary: Tell every agent two rules of this cycle: per-case records are committed packed, and a job's pass must rest on a real run
commits.body: CLAUDE.md, under Examples: an example's per-case output is committed as one cases.tar.gz a folder (the selector run packs its own; case_pack.py pack NNN packs what was left loose), the validators read a case from either, and check reports loose per-case files as an error that names the command. The operating notes, under Verification jobs: a job declares every tool its steps call and makes its pass depend on something only a real run produces, with the job of 2026-11-21 that passed in 1.2 s on 'no built native checker' as the reason; a result much faster than its estimate is read before it is believed.

commits.body: The run report named a commit that later commits of the same cycle followed; it now says where the head is found and from which commit the line is ahead of develop. The notes for the next cycle begin with the pending job 20261121-195020-345-native-selectors-with-the-built-chec and say which rehearsal folder is kept. No code changed; nothing to test.

commits.summary: Keep a session's per-call rows out of its metrics file; warn on a result's oversized receipt; seal what was set aside from the runner
commits.body:
A session's metrics.json held a row for every model call and tool call: 48 MB of the 51 MB the 207 session files come to, 9 MB in one two-day session's file, rewritten whole each time it was rendered. The file is now llm-trace-metrics/v2 (metrics.bounded): everything else it held, plus what the readers of those rows took from them (the calls by day, and for each prompt its peak context, efforts and spend by model), and 'events', the row counts and the SHA-256 of the rows' text. The rows are the same function of the log, the manifest and the price list as the file, so they are stored nowhere: 'sync.py events SESSION [--to FILE]' builds them again from the log (this workspace's, or the public URL's, checked against its name) and says whether the text is the one the file names. The roll-up and the loops' statistics read the bounded file; the roll-up is v2 and its tool rows have no median over all sessions, which cannot be had from the sessions' own.

No session file changes in this commit: an old file is still read, and the next rendering (a promotion, a push, sync by hand) rewrites each without needing its log (sync.bound_metrics); check --rendered reports one that is left. On this tree, in memory: the 207 files go from 50.9 MB to 7.2 MB (largest 1.0 MB); loops.json and loops.md come out byte for byte the same; the roll-up differs only in its schema line and the 249 absent medians; for the 180 sessions whose log is stored here, the converted file equals what a rendering from the log gives.

sync.py check warns about a verification result submitted since 2026-11-22 whose result.json is over 256 KiB (verification/layout.py, heavy_receipts). The list of outputs is left whole, since accept.py and claim_history.py verify kept outputs against every row; the receipts of 1.5 to 2.9 MB came from jobs that wrote two files a case, which the producer packs since the last cycle.

vm_inventory.py protect --only set-aside seals what a person moved out of the runner's state into restricted custody: the folder without work/ as one tree, each work directory as what it holds beyond the commit its own result names, build output left out. Run here: 2 folders (7.5 MB) and 32 work directories (130 KB beyond their commits, of 2.2 GB on disk), uploaded and read back; the archive holds 1,250 occurrences, all verified in the store.

Found on the way: test_performance's Sync test called a real rendering with only some of its steps stood in for, so since rendering was deferred it rewrote this checkout's stale summaries, and with this change every session file. It stands in for those steps now. Job 20261121-195020-345-native-selectors-with-the-built-chec passed with the built checker (collected on the default line): a selector run packs its own per-case output. Verified: the changed tests (31 files, all passed), the new unit tests of each part, and the comparisons above.

commits.summary: Seal a workspace's private run records at each sync; record cycle 3 and its rehearsal
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loop-summaries/ is never committed (its redacted copies are what is published), so a loop's private records left this machine only when someone ran vm_inventory.py protect. A sync now hands each of its files to the private archive as a stream of its own, in restricted custody (sync.seal_run_records): what the file gained since it was last sealed, or the whole of it again when it was rewritten; a file whose size and time are those last sealed is not opened; a test's folder is not this checkout's and is not sealed; an error goes to the hook log and never fails a sync. Shown by test_artifacts.py on a disk store.

The results page records cycle 3: the per-call rows out of the session files, the receipt warning, the set-aside folders sealed (my cycle 1 reading of them was wrong: each work directory's own result names its commit), the job that shows a selector run packing its own output with the real checker, and a rehearsal of the whole line on a bare remote on disk: 23 one-commit checkpoints at a median of 0.90 s and a p95 of 2.30 s from eligible commit to the remote holding it, and a promotion of 36 commits whose record rewrote all 207 session files (51.0 MB on main, 8.3 MB with the roll-up in the promoted tree) with check --rendered at 0 errors.

The operating notes gain two rules: a session's metrics.json or summary.md left conflicted by a merge is settled by rendering the session again, and a test of the trace tools writes nowhere in the checkout (the test that did is fixed in the commit before this one). A rendered check reports a file that still holds its per-call tables once, not twice. Verified: the changed tests (23 files, all passed) and jj st clean of trace files after them.

commits.summary: Give proof output one reader: a Rust contract module, a shared Python reader, and helper decisions as data
commits.body:
Part 1 of llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow.md. Three readers of the checker's --json output answered differently for the same bytes: for the first established row of example 359's selector record with only wire_version changed to 999, the ordinary decoder refused it while the native-selector check read it as established and the benchmark scored it correct; a stated.bounds.complete of the string "false" was established through Python's truthiness; and a process that exited with 2 beside a verified payload was scored correct. lib/src/proof_wire.rs now owns what prove --json and equivalence --json print (the wire version, the envelope, the exit as the maximum over a run's rows), with the command line as its caller. lib/python/jvmcontract_io.py is the one Python reader, standard library only, and keeps three questions apart: whether the bytes decode, whether the process ended as the command ends, and (the consumer's own) whether the evidence qualifies, for which it offers typed access where a missing or mistyped field is unknown.

Switched to it: ordinary ingestion (checker_output.py keeps its names and reads through it; an unreadable outcome's reason now names what the reader refused), the live native-selector check, the validation of archived selector records, and lib/benchmark/run.py, which the solver comparison reads through. A benchmark case must print its one row; a kill, an unknown version, a mistyped decision field, exit 2 and an exit that contradicts the verdict earn no score, and a valid refutation is still correct at exit 1. A new selector row records its wire version and a new record names both rule files.

A regression check under --cache now says what it did with each changed helper as data (the outcome's helpers: callee, action, the proof's claim key and whether it was found in the cache, a summary's reads and facts, a reason code). The notes in the output are rendered from the decision, word for word what they were, and the proof cache stores the decisions with a result. build.py and economics.py read the data and fall back to the notes for an outcome from before the field; their patterns never matched the two notes a summary writes. sharedHelpers still means a helper proved equal on every input.

commits.summary: Bind a proof to the class file a JVM loads: one selection in the checker, observed by a JVM, compared at launch
commits.body:
Part 2 of llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow.md. Two JARs that differ only in how the manifest spells Multi-Release's value (one line, or folded over two) load different classes on JDK 17, 21 and 25: the versioned entry of the first, the base entry of the second. The preparation took the base class of both; the Python launch guard and the Rust checker bound to release 21 took the versioned class of both, so on the folded JAR the checker refuted a property the JVM satisfies. Three parties each had a rule; now there is one selection, and it is held to a JVM.

lib/src/classpath.rs: ClassPath::bind says which class file stands for a class name on an ordered class path and the bound runtime (provider, JAR entry, SHA-256, how it was selected, every candidate, later holders), or a typed refusal with the candidates' digests and origins; every reader of class bytes in the checker goes through it. The manifest is read as the JDK's reader reads it, measured with fifteen spellings: a spelling on which that reading and the JAR specification's differ is ambiguous, and a class with a versioned entry in such a JAR is refused unless JVMCONTRACT_CLASS_OBSERVATIONS says which class file a JVM of the bound release loaded; an observation of other bytes than the rule's is a refusal with both digests. jvmcontract class-bindings answers for every side and class of a launch in one process, with whether the bound class file declares a method asked about and which entry stands for each logical name of a JAR.

examples/tools/targets/class_binding.py: the Python tools select nothing by rule. A class with one class file is read as before, and its prepared record is unchanged. A class the original artifact holds several class files of is bound at preparation by LoadedClasses on each JDK the artifact runs on (classSha256, jarEntry, classObservation); JDKs that load different bytes, another code source, or bytes no class file has are refused with both digests. Parameter lookup and every reader of a prepared entry class take the bound entry (runtime.bound_class). The native launch guard asks the checker for its bindings, one process whatever the sides and classes, and compares provider and digest with the prepared ones; the equivalence route extracts a JAR by the checker's own logical entries. A native-selector task asks once, whatever its number of selectors. runtime_jar.effective_entries stays as an inventory view for the upgrade review's tools, with the measured rule.

commits.summary: Make array induction a library method: lib/python/jvm_array_induction.py, called on a bound method and a rule (verification pending)
commits.body:
The third part of the brief llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow.md. The proof by induction over a compiled array loop was 696 lines inside one example tool. The method now lives in lib/python/jvm_array_induction.py: prove(javap, class_file, name, descriptor, rule, work, seconds) walks the method's disassembly, writes the obligations of the declared rule as one SMT query and reads Z3's answers, and knows no example, sidecar, revision or record. Reading a class file's methods from javap is lib/python/jvm_disassembly.py, which the schedule and monitor experiments now import instead of the proof method's module. examples/tools/targets/array_induction.py is left as the adapter: it finds the declared contract, takes the revision, prepares the artifacts, refuses a class whose initializer the rule does not qualify, and publishes the record. Cell width comes from the descriptor and the rule from the contract, with no switch on an example.

A record made from now on (java-array-induction-result/v2) names the rule implementation under rules: each file of the rule and the adapter by digest, and one digest over them. The fifteen stored records keep rulesSha256, the digest of the adapter file when it held the method too, and are read as before; rules_of reads either format. No stored record was rewritten and none was added.

The organic benchmark's baseline fingerprint and frozen export (lib/benchmark/organic-java/run.py) listed paths under lib/src, lib/models and examples/tools only, so code under lib/python was outside both. They are now versioned inventories that a pin names (inputs): a pin without the key is inventory 1 and is fingerprinted and exported exactly as before; inventory 2, for a new baseline, adds lib/python and verification/layout.py, which the example tools load at import (an export without it did not start since the process-plumbing run). The existing pin is unchanged.

Verified: each of the five declared contracts (336 first-any-length; 337 fill-any-length, caller-any-length and the negative control caller-extra-any-length; 346 first-any-length with 64-bit cells) proved again through the extracted method and compared with its stored record differs in no field: obligations with expected and obtained answers, widths, class digests, bytecode, certificate digest, status. The control stays unresolved on 'caller read follows from the proved frame' (expected unsat, obtained sat). That comparison is a new mode, build.py NNN --array-induction CONTRACT --compare, which writes nothing to the example; job 20261121-220624-array-induction-through-the-library-meth runs the five at this commit. New tests: lib/python/test_jvm_array_induction.py (6: a search compiled in the test, established for int and long cells, not established when it reads past the end, refused for a rule it does not fit), examples/tools/targets/test_array_induction.py (3) and lib/benchmark/organic-java/test_run.py (4: the pinned revision exported by its inventory has the pin's 224 files and fingerprint; a change to the extracted module alone changes inventory 2's fingerprint and not inventory 1's; a frozen export run with python3 -I loads its own reader and rules). test_costs.py run --changed passed 43 of 43, and examples 336, 337, 346, 342 and 343 pass validate_example.py.

lib/README.md gains an Array induction section and the ownership map's row for proof methods now names the library module and its test. llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow-results.md records part 3 and the brief's exit: both reproducers with their corrected outcomes, the consumers of the extracted method, the historical readings, one more process for a native launch and for a selector task (18 to 29 ms) and none elsewhere, and 0.59 s before against 0.55 s after to read example 359's archived selectors.

commits.body:
Job 20261121-221235-the-proof-tier-after-the-proof-output-mo runs the proof tier of the Rust tests, with cargo's --no-fail-fast and without the three heap tests VF-018 tracks, as the jobs after examples 287 and 288 did. Parts 1 and 2 of the run of llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow.md changed what every proof-tier test goes through: what prove --json and equivalence --json print and how a run exits (lib/src/proof_wire.rs, with a cached regression check's helper decisions as data), and every reading of a class's bytes in the checker (ClassPath::bind and read_class in lib/src/classpath.rs). The unit and tool tiers passed at each of those commits; the proof tier runs only as a job.

The results page llm-dlc/loops/lib-architecture-fast-follow-results.md lists this job and the array-induction one under what is queued. Nothing else changed, so no test was run for this commit.
